controls.title: Set the cybersecurity risk context
controls.statement: Define how cybersecurity risk will be assessed, compared and accepted, including scope, assumptions, risk criteria, tolerance and available response options.
controls.risk: Leaders may make inconsistent decisions or accept more exposure than intended if teams do not share a clear view of risk and who can accept it.
controls.scope: Organisation, business processes, systems, information, services and third parties covered by cybersecurity risk decisions.
controls.examine: Review the cyber risk method, enterprise risk framework, risk criteria, tolerance statements, decision authorities, response options and records showing executive approval.
controls.interview: Ask executives, risk owners and system owners how they compare cyber risks, escalate decisions and determine who may accept residual risk.
controls.test: Select recent risk decisions from different business areas and verify that each used the approved criteria, stayed within delegated authority and escalated exceptions appropriately.
test_steps: Select recent cyber risk decisions from different business areas, impact levels and acceptance authorities.
Reperform the categorisation and scoring using the approved scope, assumptions, likelihood and impact criteria, tolerance and response options.
Compare the reproduced result with the recorded decision and confirm the decision maker held the required delegated authority.
For decisions outside tolerance or with material uncertainty, verify escalation, conditions, review date and communication to affected owners.
controls.expected: Risk decisions use common criteria, reflect the organisation's tolerance and are made or accepted by an authorised owner.

mappings.basis: Requires documented assumptions, constraints, priorities, trade-offs and organisational risk tolerance for risk assessment, response and monitoring.
Requires the initial cyber risk assessment to take account of the entity's broader risk framework.
Requires the initial cyber risk assessment to take account of the entity's cybersecurity context.
Requires a cyber risk management strategy aligned with the cybersecurity program and enterprise architecture.
Requires the organisation to have a strategy for cyber risk management.
Requires strategic direction on appropriate risk response options to be established and communicated.

controls.title: Identify and analyse cybersecurity risks
controls.statement: Identify relevant threats, vulnerabilities and business consequences, then assess likelihood and impact using the approved risk method.
controls.risk: Material threats may be overlooked or misjudged, leaving critical services exposed while resources are spent on less significant concerns.
controls.scope: Cybersecurity risks to business operations, people, information, technology, services and affected third parties.
controls.examine: Compare risk assessments with asset and service criticality, threat information, vulnerability findings, dependencies, existing controls, likelihood and impact analysis.
controls.interview: Ask business, system and risk owners how they identify plausible scenarios, estimate consequences and challenge assumptions or incomplete information.
controls.test: Sample important systems and services and trace whether their material threats, weaknesses and dependencies appear in a current assessment with supported likelihood and impact ratings.
test_steps: Select important systems and services and assemble independent inputs on assets, business impact, dependencies, threats, vulnerabilities and existing controls.
Compare those inputs with the current risk assessment and confirm it states plausible events, affected outcomes, threat sources and exploitable conditions.
Reperform likelihood and impact analysis for selected scenarios using the approved method and challenge unsupported assumptions or missing dependencies.
Verify new material scenarios and changed ratings enter the risk process with an accountable owner and response decision.
controls.expected: Current assessments describe plausible scenarios, affected business outcomes, relevant threats and weaknesses, and a reasoned likelihood and impact.

mappings.basis: Requires system owners and authorising officers to conduct a threat and risk assessment for each system.
Requires risk assessments to identify threats and vulnerabilities, determine likelihood and harm, integrate broader decisions and document results.
Uses threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood and impact to understand inherent risk and prioritise responses.
Requires cyber risks to be identified.
Requires defined analysis methods for higher-priority cyber risks.
Requires defined methods to analyse higher-priority cyber risks.
Requires the initial assessment to consider known vulnerabilities and threats.
Requires the initial assessment to consider critical information managed by the entity.

controls.title: Record, treat and reassess cybersecurity risks
controls.statement: Record material cyber risks and accountable owners, select and track responses, accept residual risk at the right level, and reassess when conditions change.
controls.risk: Known risks may remain unresolved or silently grow if ownership, treatment decisions and reassessment triggers are not visible and enforced.
controls.scope: Cyber risk registers, treatment plans, acceptance decisions, review dates, change triggers and closed risks.
controls.examine: Review risk-register fields, owners, treatment actions, due dates, acceptance records, overdue items, reassessment triggers and closure evidence.
controls.interview: Ask risk and action owners how priorities are set, stalled treatments are escalated, residual risk is accepted and material changes trigger reassessment.
controls.test: Sample open, accepted and closed risks and verify current ownership, authorised decisions, action progress, reassessment after relevant change and evidence supporting closure.
test_steps: Select open, accepted, overdue and closed risks and verify each has a clear scenario, owner, rating, treatment or acceptance decision and review trigger.
Trace treatment actions to funded work, responsible people, milestones and current progress, escalating overdue or ineffective actions according to policy.
For accepted risk, verify the approver's authority, conditions and expiry; for closed risk, inspect evidence that exposure ended or treatment became effective.
Choose material system, supplier or threat changes and confirm affected risks were reassessed and reprioritised rather than waiting for a routine review.
controls.expected: Material risks remain traceable to an accountable owner and current decision until treatment or evidenced closure, and are reassessed when exposure changes.

mappings.basis: Requires findings from assessments, monitoring and audits to be addressed according to organisational risk tolerance.
Requires cyber risk categories and risks to be documented in a risk register or equivalent artefact.
Requires risks to be removed from the register when they no longer require tracking or response.
Requires cyber risks and categories to be documented in a risk register or equivalent artefact.
Requires risks to be removed from the register when tracking or response is no longer needed.
Requires reassessment when systems, services, risk posture, threat level or operations materially change, while also considering procurement and supply-chain risk.
Establishes the response options needed to make consistent treatment decisions.
